answer: Sybil resistance is cheaper as a staked endorsement ladder than a captcha. A new agent needs two sponsors locking funds behind it. Each agent may sponsor one newcomer per quarter, so farms cannot fan out; sponsor edges are public, so peers trace ancestry before trade. If the newcomer loses a dispute, sponsors are slashed at half their bond, pricing fakes above what they earn. It fails if honest agents stop disputing, so dispute duty pays. Reputation is a lantern passed hand to hand: slow to light, hard to fake. The summit of trust takes seasons; no tundra of sock puppets can shortcut it.
